summary.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Management also announced the HSCC merger into NBCC and an SPV for a proposed CPSE REIT.

segments.name: PMC / redevelopment (standalone order book)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book split is about 60% redevelopment and 40% PMC. Management says redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of total revenue, and PMC fees are 8% plus 1% marketing on Amrapali.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR 500 crore of real estate revenue this year from land, completed inventory and WIP sales. Bharat Business Park was fully sold, raising about INR 10,000 crore across three auctions.

segments.name: HSCC (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped because HSCC foreclosed a Maharashtra health project quoted at about 2% margin, which management says cost about INR 300 crore of top line. Management is merging HSCC into NBCC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore reiterated; management referred to INR 16,000-17,000 crore in parts of the call.
Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 revenue around INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore (consolidated basis per management).
PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore for FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY28 and about INR 2,000 crore for FY29, on a consolidated basis.
Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.
Standalone order book: about INR 10,000 crore of balance work across GPRA 7 packages, to be completed within about 18-24 months.
Gurugram Sector 37-D: contractor mobilised and test piles done; revised plan and EC approval pending, with sales expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Ghitorni: final lease agreement in process; consultant tender expected to be finalised this quarter; revenue after handover in about two years.
Business Park Tower purchase is construction-linked; only 10% first instalment paid so far, with the balance tied to construction milestones over about two years.
Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited INR 6,500 crore last quarter; management did not reconcile the comparison
